text:
maria.infra: Seeing repeated p95 spikes between gpu-rack-07 and gpu-rack-09 during the 120-180s batching window. p95 goes from 2.3ms to ~55-120ms for east-west sockets.
kevin.sre: Ugh. Any packet loss counters or retransmit rates?
maria.infra: Yep, we see small but consistent increases in tx_dropped and rx_errors on node NICs. RDMA CQE errors on the infra dashboard too.
anya-ml: Which model workload? Larger seq lengths or just request rate?
maria.infra: It's during our highest concurrency jobs (seq 1024, continuous batching). CPU not saturated, GPU queues look fine; KV cache hit ratio stable. Problem aligns with high fanout between those two racks.
jonah-l: Can you paste ethtool/SNMP stats?
maria.infra: Here's a quick dump:
```
ethtool -S ens11f0 | grep -E "tx_dropped|rx_errors|rx_crc_errors"
tx_dropped: 12
rx_errors: 0
rx_crc_errors: 3
``` 
maria.infra: Also seeing intermittent neighbor timeouts on the ip neigh table
```
ip -s -s neigh show nud failed
10.10.72.34 dev ens11f0 lladdr xx:yy:zz REACHABLE 10
```
kevin.sre: rx_crc_errors + neighbor failures -> possible MTU/jumbo mismatch or bad switch port. Any config changes/deploys around the time window?
maria.infra: No infra deploys; last change was a firmware rollout to rack06 earlier in the week, but racks 07/09 untouched.
deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance: nic-firmware-rollout -> rack07 at 2026-03-22T02:00Z (automated)
anya-ml: Could be ECMP causing reordering when large batches spread across flows. Reordering can blow up RDMA and TCP latency.
jonah-l: Can we get a pcap for the 2-3 minute window? Also run `ethtool -k` to check offloads (GRO/TSO/LRO) on both ends.
maria.infra: Captured pcap + tcpdump filter saved to s3://infra-debug/pcap-1790123456.pcap.gz. Offloads look identical on both nodes, but GRO flapping when congestion spikes.
kevin.sre: Temp mitigation: 1) Reduce batch accumulation window from 200ms->120ms for affected jobs (lowers fanout). 2) Pin cross-rack traffic to single preferred path via policy route to avoid ECMP reordering.
anya-ml: Tradeoff: reducing batch window increases per-token cost by ~8-12% but improves tail latency.
maria.infra: Implemented route pinning on a test node and throttled batch window for canary pool. Observed p95 drop back to ~3-4ms.
jonah-l: Plan: collect full ethtool -S, rdma error logs, and switch port counters. If switch shows fc/tx errors -> hardware swap. If not, schedule NIC fw rollout to racks 07/09.
kevin.sre: I'll open a hardware ticket if port errors exist. Also let's enable enhanced logging for RDMA on the next ramp.
maria.infra: Will attach graphs + pcap to the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup: 
nic-monitor-bot: Alert resolved for canary pool after route pinning and batch window reduction. Duration: 00:42:17
maria.infra: Keeping this thread for postmortem notes. Next steps: run scheduled fw rollout on rack07 if switch checks clean, otherwise swap port. Also check MTU across the leaf-agg path.
kevin.sre: Note: add MTU verification to onboarding checklist for new racks.
anya-ml: And we'll add a failover policy in planner to fallback to lower-fanout mode when p95 > 20ms.
jonah-l: I'll draft the postmortem and include perf/cost analysis.
